t: 2786. Visit Array Positions to Maximize Score
o: We walk indices in increasing order (any subset, visited in order) collecting nums[i], paying x whenever consecutive visited values differ in parity. This is a classic parity DP: track the best score of a visit sequence ending at an even value and one ending at an odd value. Processing left to right, for each element the best sequence ending here is nums[i] plus either the best same-parity tail (no penalty) or the best opposite-parity tail minus x. Example 1: nums=[2,3,6,1,9], x=5 — visiting 2,6,1,9 pays one penalty, scoring 13.
k: Only the parity of the last visited value matters for future decisions — a 2-state DP suffices.
dp[e], dp[o] = best score of any valid sequence ending with an even/odd value; update in one pass.

a.i: Maintain best[2]: the maximum score obtainable by a sequence ending in each parity. Initialize with nums[0] in its parity slot (and −infinity conceptually elsewhere, handled by initializing both to nums[0]−x style baselines). For each subsequent value, candidate = v + max(best[same], best[other] − x); update best and the global answer.
s: Initialize best[parity of nums[0]] = nums[0]; answer = nums[0].
For each later v: cur = v + max(best[v%2], best[1−v%2] − x); update best[v%2] = max(best[v%2], cur) and answer = max(answer, cur).

c.python:
class Solution:
    def maxScore(self, nums: List[int], x: int) -> int:
        best = [nums[0], nums[0]]
        best[nums[0] & 1 ^ 1] -= x
        ans = nums[0]
        for v in nums[1:]:
            p = v & 1
            cur = v + max(best[p], best[p ^ 1] - x)
            best[p] = max(best[p], cur)
            ans = max(ans, cur)
        return ans

a.t: O(n) — single pass with constant work per element

w: Return type is long in C++/Java since scores can reach ~1e11. Note you may stop anywhere — hence tracking the global max over all 'cur', not just the final state. A common pitfall is forcing visits of all elements; skipping is allowed and often optimal when x is large. Follow-up: what if penalties depended on the actual values rather than parity? Then you'd need a different state design.
